summary: Internal Q2 roadmap launch readiness meeting; reviewed recent incident affecting Redwood Dedicated deployments, identified root cause related to KV cache eviction under burst load + a scheduling bug. Agreed on immediate mitigations, canary rollout plan, and a set of action items: postmortem, load tests, canary plan, and updates to launch checklist and playbooks. Decided to increase infra burst quota for canary and tighten alert thresholds. Follow-ups scheduled with owners and due-dates.
transcript:
[10:30:01] Ava Martinez: ok everyone thanks for joining, we're doing the roadmap launch readiness plus the incident review so let's try to keep to the agenda, about 75 minutes, lots to cover
[10:30:15] Liam Chen: yep, thanks Ava, quick note i got the recent logs, i can share the link after the call, S3 link is in the doc, but top-level the outage was KV cache pressure causing a spike in p99 token latency, then scheduler retries made it worse
[10:30:42] Sofia Patel: and just to add, the eviction code path raced with the sharding scheduler so some connections got double-evicted, we saw reconnections pile up
[10:31:08] Emma Johnson: can you spell that again, double-evict? like evict then reconnect then evict again?
[10:31:20] Sofia Patel: yeah so the worker reclaimed slots, then the scheduler immediately reassigned without warming the kv, so we had a cold start on hot prefixes, it amplified latency
[10:31:45] Noah Rivera: is this specific to a quantized model or all models?
[10:31:57] Sofia Patel: mostly seen on Dedicated GPU pools with high concurrency and large seq len; quantization made memory smaller but pressure still hits at scale
[10:32:20] Ava Martinez: ok thanks, let's move through the agenda, first root cause summary, then mitigations, then canary plan and launch checklist gaps, then action items
[10:32:36] Liam Chen: root cause recap \u2014 scheduling race + KV eviction under burst traffic; secondary contributor was our autoscaler thresholds being too permissive so we didn't pre-warm nodes fast enough
[10:32:55] Emma Johnson: timeline: the incident started at 02:12 UTC, lasted about 18 minutes, with p99 at 4.2s at peak, affecting about 6 customer clusters, not full outage but significant errors and retries
[10:33:18] Sofia Patel: that's right; we also had a metric mislabeling that delayed alerting by ~4 minutes, that made on-call slower to react
[10:33:37] Kai Zhou: note \u2014 metric mislabeling is in the alert rule for scheduler_retries, I opened a PR to fix it but didn't merge yet
[10:33:50] Ava Martinez: ok we should merge that asap, that becomes an action item, Kai can you take that?
[10:34:01] Kai Zhou: yep I'll take it, will merge and roll out within the hour
[10:34:22] Noah Rivera: user impact note \u2014 CS reported two customers who saw timeouts during nightly batch jobs, one had a fallback to smaller batch which succeeded, other retried and hit customer-side rate limits
[10:34:44] Emma Johnson: that matches the logs, and there was also a side effect where cache warming didn't happen because of a race in the pre-warm path
[10:35:05] Liam Chen: mitigation ideas \u2014 short-term: tighten eviction threshold, revert aggressive autoscaler change, and increase burst quotas for canary; medium-term: fix scheduler race and introduce async warming
[10:35:28] Sofia Patel: also add metric labels and an alert variant for kv_eviction_count > X in 1 min so on-call is notified earlier
[10:35:45] Ava Martinez: ok now the roadmap impact \u2014 we were planning to launch the new Dedicated scaling feature next week, is that still safe?
[10:35:58] Emma Johnson: we need at least a canary with reduced traffic and the rollback playbook; if we can't get the scheduler fix in ear-ly canary we'll delay by one week, but we can still do a limited soft launch for internal teams
[10:36:20] Liam Chen: I propose we run a 72-hour load test on the dedicated pool with synthetic traffic that includes hot prefix patterns, then iterate on thresholds before canary
[10:36:36] Noah Rivera: SLA risk assessment \u2014 if we delay one week we should notify sales and customers with affected timelines, also update the roadmap page
[10:36:50] Ava Martinez: make that an owner item, Noah please draft the customer comms template
[10:37:02] Noah Rivera: yep will do, will share draft by EOD tomorrow
[10:37:18] Kai Zhou: infra ask \u2014 we'll need a temporary burst quota increase to run the canary, request to cloud team is in the ticket, awaiting approval
[10:37:33] Emma Johnson: for canary we also need automated rollback: if p99 > 2s for more than 10 minutes we rollback, and if error rate > 0.5% we rollback \u2014 we should codify thresholds in the runbook
[10:37:56] Sofia Patel: agreed, and add a health-check for KV cache hit ratio and scheduler_retry spikes
[10:38:10] Liam Chen: small note: our bench harness underestimates concurrency because it uses smaller seq lengths; we need to replicate real customer seq distribution
[10:38:27] Ava Martinez: action item: Liam to update bench harness and run it for 72 hours
[10:38:40] Emma Johnson: also add circuit-breaker testing \u2014 simulate node flaps during the warm-up period
[10:38:55] Noah Rivera: anything from legal or security? not in this call but if canary touches customer data we need to ensure KMS keys and audit logs are set for the canary environment
[10:39:12] Sophia: (speech recognition flips name) sorry that's Sofia, good point \u2014 we'll ensure all KMS and audit logging is enabled for canary private deployments, and run a small audit before canary
[10:39:29] Ava Martinez: good, note that Private/VPC customers require additional approvals; for dedicated customers it's internal but still need proper logging
[10:39:43] Liam Chen: ok timeline proposal: today-overnight fix for alert labeling and merge; 24-48 hours run bench updates and start 72h load test; canary rollout on 2026-04-26 with scaled down traffic; full launch targeted 2026-05-03 pending no regressions
[10:40:05] Emma Johnson: that seems reasonable, but we need sign-off from infra and SRE on the 24h results
[10:40:18] Kai Zhou: infra sign-off will be done in the ticket, I'll ping infra owners and get a firm yes/no by 2026-04-25
